Remove duplicate sequences

Source: R/fasta.R
dereplicate.Rd

Keeps the first copy of every distinct sequence, like `seqkit rmdup -s`.

Usage

dereplicate(x, both_strands = TRUE)

Arguments

x

A named character vector of sequences, or a path to a FASTA file.

both_strands

If `TRUE` (default), a sequence and its reverse complement count as duplicates.

Value

A named character vector with duplicates removed.

Details

Be careful when de-replicating a *reference* ("good") database that is used by [clean_reference()]: if two genera share an identical sequence, keeping only one copy hides exactly the ambiguity that the "matches multiple genus" check is designed to detect. De-replicating the contaminant database is harmless.

Examples

seqs <- c(a = "ACGTT", b = "ACGTT", c = "AACGT", d = "GGGCC")
dereplicate(seqs)
#>       a       d 
#> "ACGTT" "GGGCC" 
dereplicate(seqs, both_strands = FALSE)
#>       a       c       d 
#> "ACGTT" "AACGT" "GGGCC"
